subject: Archaeology
title: The Flood Tablet: Gilgamesh and the Bible
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Flood Tablet: Gilgamesh and the Bible.

hook.text: In 1872, George Smith found a clay tablet describing a great flood — and the story was older than the Bible by.

buildup.text: Tablet XI of Gilgamesh describes Utnapishtim building a boat, loading animals, surviving a flood, and releasing a dove.

discovery.text: The parallels to Noah are unmistakable: divine warning, a boat, a flood, animals, a dove, and a landing on a mountain.

twist.text: The discovery shook Victorian England. If the Bible's flood story was borrowed from Babylon, what else was not original?

climax.text: The Daily Telegraph funded Smith's trip to Nineveh to find the missing piece of the tablet — and incredibly.

punchline.text: A newspaper paid an archaeologist to find one tablet shard in Iraq's rubble.

quiz.question: Why did the Flood Tablet discovery shock Victorian England?
options: It proved that all ancient civilizations experienced the same flood
It showed the Bible's flood story was borrowed from a much older Babylonian tale
It contained a prediction of future floods that seemed to be coming true
